q: The idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was first put forward by:
explanation: M.N. Roy, a pioneer of the communist movement, first put forward the idea in 1934. Nehru's demand came in 1938 (as INC's official position). Gandhi did not propose it. Ambedkar entered the picture in the 1940s as a member and later Drafting Committee chairman.

q: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, the total strength of the Constituent Assembly was fixed at:
explanation: 389 = 292 (governors' provinces) + 4 (Chief Commissioners' provinces) + 93 (princely states). 299 is the strength AFTER partition (reduced); 211 is the attendance on the first day (9 Dec 1946) with the Muslim League boycott; 385 is a fabricated trap number.

q: Who was appointed the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly at its first meeting on 9 December 1946?
explanation: Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member (from Arrah, Bihar), was appointed temporary President on 9 Dec 1946. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 Dec 1946 — the classic trap. B.N. Rau was Constitutional Adviser. H.C. Mukherjee was a Vice-President of the Assembly.

q: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on:
explanation: The Assembly adopted (passed) the Constitution on 26 Nov 1949; some provisions (citizenship, elections, provisional parliament) came into force immediately. The remaining provisions commenced on 26 Jan 1950, commemorating Purna Swaraj Day 1930.

q: The Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly was set up on 29 August 1947 with how many members?
explanation: The Drafting Committee had 7 members chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar: B.R. Ambedkar, N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rao (replaced B.L. Mitter) and T.T. Krishnamachari (replaced D.P. Khaitan after his death). '9' is the common trap.

q: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee?
explanation: Sardar Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee and the Advisory Committee on FRs & Minorities, but was never on the Drafting Committee. Its seven members: Ambedkar (chair), N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rao and T.T. Krishnamachari.

q: Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly: 1. It was elected directly by adult franchise. 2. Its seats were allotted to provinces roughly in the ratio of one per ten lakh population. 3. The Muslim League boycotted its first meeting on 9 December 1946. Which is/are correct?
explanation: Statement 1 is WRONG: the Assembly was indirectly elected by provincial legislative assemblies on a limited franchise — a standard BPSC trap. Statement 2 is correct (ratio 1:10 lakh). Statement 3 is correct — the ML boycotted the first sitting; only 211 of 389 attended.

q: Match List-I (feature) with List-II (source Constitution): (a) Concurrent List (b) DPSP (c) Fundamental Rights (d) Amendment procedure — 1) USA 2) Australia 3) Ireland 4) South Africa
explanation: Concurrent List ← Australia; DPSP ← Ireland; Fundamental Rights ← USA; amendment procedure ← South Africa. Japan gave 'procedure established by law' (Art 21); Canada gave federation-with-strong-Centre + residuary powers; USSR gave Fundamental Duties.

q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched? (Feature — Source)
options: Method of election of the President — Britain
explanation: The method of election of the President (single-transferable-vote electoral college) was borrowed from the Irish Constitution, not Britain. Britain contributed parliamentary government, single citizenship, CAG, writs, etc. Classic 'NOT matched' style used by BPSC on Schedules (70th) and sources alike.

q: The Constitution, as adopted on 26 November 1949, consisted of:
explanation: As adopted: 395 Articles in 22 Parts + 8 Schedules. Today, after amendments, it is ~448 Articles in 25 Parts + 12 Schedules (the present-day figures are the exam trap). Schedules 9-12 were added by the 1st (1951), 42nd (1976), 73rd (1992) and 74th (1992) amendments respectively.

q: The Constituent Assembly took how long to frame the Constitution?
explanation: 9 Dec 1946 → 26 Nov 1949 = 2 years, 11 months, 18 days, across 11 sessions, at a cost of ₹64 lakh. 7,632 amendments were tabled; about 2,473 were actually discussed. '2y 11m 6d' is the classic near-miss trap.

q: The first sitting of the Constituent Assembly was presided over by Sachchidananda Sinha and the Assembly's Constitutional Adviser was:
explanation: Sir B.N. Rau prepared the working draft of the Constitution as Constitutional Adviser. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee (created Aug 1947, after Rau's draft). Alladi and Munshi were Drafting Committee members — note the adviser vs drafting-body distinction.

q: Consider the following criticisms levelled against the Constituent Assembly: 1. It was not elected on the basis of universal adult franchise. 2. It was created under the Cabinet Mission Plan and was initially not fully sovereign. 3. It was dominated by Gandhian village-level workers. Which are valid?
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are classic criticisms: indirect election on limited franchise, and birth under the Cabinet Mission Plan rather than as a fully sovereign body. Statement 3 is the opposite of the truth — the Assembly was criticised for NOT reflecting the Gandhian village ideal; Art 40 was the only concession.

q: The Constituent Assembly doubled as the Dominion Legislature (1947–49) and then the Provisional Parliament (26 Jan 1950 onwards) until the first Lok Sabha met in:
explanation: The first Lok Sabha was constituted in 1952 after the first general election (1951–52). Until then the Assembly functioned as the Dominion Legislature (1947–49) and then the Provisional Parliament (1950–52). Options B and C confuse the commencement of the Constitution (1950) and the election announcement (1951).

q: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains provisions regarding the anti-defection law?
explanation: The 10th Schedule (added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985) contains the anti-defection provisions under Art 102(2)/191(2). 8th = 22 languages; 9th = land-reform validations (1st Amendment 1951; immunity curtailed by I.R. Coelho, 2007); 11th = Panchayats (73rd Amendment).

q: Which pair is NOT correctly matched? (Schedule — Subject)
options: Allocation of seats in Council of States — 4th Schedule
explanation: Languages are in the 8th Schedule (22 languages), NOT the 9th (land-reform acts). The 70th BPSC asked exactly this 'NOT matched' pattern on Schedules. The 9th Schedule's immunity was curtailed by I.R. Coelho (2007) — post-24 Apr 1973 laws are open to judicial review.

q: The permanent President of the Constituent Assembly, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, was elected on:
explanation: Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 December 1946, two days after the first sitting. Note the Bihar link: both the temporary and permanent Presidents of the Assembly were from Bihar (Sinha from Arrah, Prasad from Siwan).

q: Which of the following features was borrowed from the Constitution of Japan?
options: Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency
explanation: 'Procedure established by law' (Art 21) comes from Japan. Concurrent List is Australia; the ideal of justice is USSR (Preamble); suspension of FRs during Emergency is Germany (Weimar Art 48 model → Arts 358–359).

q: Match the committees of the Constituent Assembly with their chairmen: (a) Union Powers Committee (b) Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights & Minorities (c) Steering Committee (d) Drafting Committee — 1) Dr. Rajendra Prasad 2) Jawaharlal Nehru 3) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar 4) Sardar Patel
explanation: Union Powers → Nehru; Advisory on FRs & Minorities → Patel; Steering → Rajendra Prasad; Drafting → Ambedkar. Extra: Union Constitution Committee → Nehru; Provincial Constitution Committee → Patel; States Committee → Nehru. A frequent BPSC matching pattern.

q: Consider the statements about the Objectives Resolution: 1. It was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946. 2. It proclaimed India an 'Independent Sovereign Republic'. 3. It later formed the basis of the Preamble. Which is/are correct?
explanation: All three are correct. Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 Dec 1946; it was adopted on 22 Jan 1947; it proclaimed India an Independent Sovereign Republic and became the basis (in spirit) of the Preamble. Links directly to Topic 39.

q: The 26th of January was chosen as the commencement date of the Constitution to commemorate:
options: The coming into force of the Government of India Act, 1935
explanation: 26 Jan commemorates Purna Swaraj Day, first celebrated 26 Jan 1930 following the Lahore session resolution (Dec 1929). Adoption was 26 Nov 1949. Gandhi's return was 9 Jan 1915. The GoI Act 1935 is the source of much administrative machinery but not of the date.

q: Which of the following statements about the Constituent Assembly is/are correct? 1. The Assembly held 11 sessions over 2 years, 11 months and 18 days. 2. The Assembly's first item of business was the appointment of Sachchidananda Sinha as temporary President. 3. The Assembly adopted the Flag of the Dominion of India on 22 July 1947.
explanation: All correct. 11 sessions; temporary President appointed at the first sitting; the Assembly adopted the national flag design on 22 July 1947 (Pingali Venkayya's design with the Ashoka Chakra replacing the charkha). Also note: the Assembly ratified India's membership of the Commonwealth in May 1949.

q: The Objectives Resolution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on:
explanation: Moved 13 Dec 1946 (by Nehru), adopted 22 Jan 1947. 29 Aug 1947 is the Drafting Committee formation date. The moved/adopted distinction is a classic BPSC trap.

q: Consider the following statements: 1. The Constitution of India was framed by the Constituent Assembly set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946. 2. The Constituent Assembly was created by an Act of the British Parliament. 3. The Assembly elected its permanent President on 11 December 1946. Which of the above is/are correct?
explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the Assembly was set up under the Cabinet Mission Plan (May 1946). Statement 2 is wrong: it was NOT created by an Act of the British Parliament — a favourite BPSC trap. Statement 3 is correct: Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent President on 11 Dec 1946.

q: Match the years with events in the making of the Constitution: (a) M.N. Roy's idea (b) August Offer (c) First sitting of the Assembly (d) Adoption of the Constitution — 1) 1949 2) 1946 3) 1940 4) 1934
explanation: (a) 1934 (M.N. Roy), (b) 1940 (August Offer), (c) 1946 (first sitting 9 Dec), (d) 1949 (adoption 26 Nov). Chronological-ladder questions are BPSC staples. Memorise the year chain: 34-38-40-42-46-47-49-50.
